title: A full-screen recording with Mac sound and the microphone plays the moment you stop it
goal: A full-screen recording that takes sound from both the Mac and the microphone can only play once macOS finishes its file, and that takes about half as long as the recording itself (20 seconds for a 45 second recording). The window opens on the last frame at once, but Play, Copy and the corner card wait. Make it playable right away, the way a recording with one sound source already is (under 100 ms).
notes: Measured 2026-10-10 on the probe after the fix in a-recording-is-in-history-and-opens-the-instant: SCRecordingOutput (ScreenRecorder.swift) with captureMicrophone AND capturesAudio on a full 3456x2234 display reports recordingOutputDidFinishRecording at 1.58-1.64 s (3 s, n=10), 4.52-4.67 s (10 s, n=10), 20.0 s (45 s, n=3). Same sound on a 480x300 region: 52-85 ms. Either source alone at full screen: 22-75 ms. So the close cost scales with video size only when both audio sources are on, suggesting SCRecordingOutput rewrites the file to mix the two audio tracks. Ideas: record the mic through its own SCStreamOutput / AVAssetWriter audio track and mix later, or write the whole file with AVAssetWriter. The user records with audio=3 (both), see defaults photonz.recordingConfig.
acceptance: A 45 s full-screen recording with Mac sound and microphone is playable in the editor within 1 s of Stop, measured with Scripts/recording-latency-drill.sh 45 --system-audio --with-microphone
The finished file still has both sounds mixed and in sync with the picture
3 s and 10 s recordings with both sources are playable within 300 ms of Stop
Recordings with one or no sound source are no slower than today (under 100 ms to land)

log.note: Reproduced 2026-10-11 on the probe: Scripts/recording-latency-drill.sh 10 --system-audio --with-microphone -> file closed by macOS 4630 ms, editor playable 4646 ms. Container is not the cause: outputFileType .mov still closes at 4630 ms and still writes one mixed AAC track. Experiment: a passthrough remux (AVAssetReader->AVAssetWriter, no re-encode) of picture + one audio track takes 23 ms for a 10 s full-screen file and 46 ms for the user's 45 s one, with identical frame times and colour tags. Plan: when both sounds are on, SCRecordingOutput records picture + Mac sound only (the fast-closing case), the microphone is captured with AVCaptureSession, both are mixed live on the host clock and encoded to an AAC side file while recording, and Stop copies picture + mixed sound into the final file. Behind a new Next flag on by default; any failure falls back to the picture file with Mac sound so a recording is never lost. Adversarial: a person sees no new UI, only Play/Copy ready sooner; risks are sync (verified by cross-correlating against SCK's own Mac-sound track) and the mic's first moments if AVCaptureSession starts later than the first frame (measured below).

Built: SoundMixTimeline (PhotonzCore, 14 tests), RecordingSoundWriter + RecordingSoundMerge + PCMSamples (PhotonzMedia, 7 tests), RecordingSoundMixer (app) wired into ScreenRecorder's cold start and stop, behind next-two-sounds-mixed-as-you-record (on at Next defaults; Current keeps macOS mixing). Verified on the probe with Scripts/recording-latency-drill.sh at full screen, both sounds: editor playable 60 ms (3 s), 46 ms (10 s), 92 ms (45 s); system only 25 ms, mic only 49 ms, none 49 ms. Sync: Tink onsets 1.4523/4.3729/7.2910/10.2002 s identical in SCK's own Mac-sound track, the live mix and the joined file; mic buffers arrive 12 ms after their converted host-clock stamp; mic room noise (peak 0.0016) present in the joined file. Walks: a-recording-stays-and-opens-right-after-stop-walk ok (files land 73-107 ms after Stop), the-recording-control-stays-where-you-put-it-walk ok. Tests: full run hung in the known Vision/HEIF stall (logged on find-out-why-the-whole-test-run-hangs-in-the-mac); split run green 11212 + 1143 + 118.

left rough: the microphone is first heard ~85 ms after the first frame (AVCaptureSession opens in parallel with the stream), so a recording's first tenth of a second has no voice. Did not earn a task: nobody has reported it and it is under a syllable; could be closed by opening the mic while the recording card is up. Also left: the stop-then-open walk no longer sees any file still closing at 0.2 s (0 of 20), so at Next defaults it now proves landing speed rather than opening mid-close; PlaytestOpenAtStop still forces a 3 s close for that.

With Mac sound and the microphone both on, the recorder now mixes them live while recording (Next switch next-two-sounds-mixed-as-you-record, on by default) and joins pictures + mix at Stop without re-encoding. Probe drill, full screen, both sounds: playable 60 ms after Stop for 3 s, 46 ms for 10 s, 92 ms for 45 s (were 1.6 s, 4.6 s, 20 s); one or no sound unchanged at 25-49 ms. Mac sound sync matches macOS's own track to 0.1 ms; mic stamps on the host clock (arrive 12 ms after).
